campaign_spec.critical_open_problem: Does future admissibility organization depend on accumulated prior deviations, or is it strictly determined by the immediately preceding state (Markov vs. Non-Markov)?

hypothesis.statement: Future admissibility organization depends on accumulated prior deviations rather than only the immediately previous state.

test_design.description: Examine divergence of full-history runs compared to last-state-only, shuffled, and truncated controls.

tests.name: Last State Control
tests.description: Admissibility transition relies only on the immediately prior state.

tests.name: History Shuffle Control
tests.description: The sequence of historical admissibility changes is randomized prior to transition evaluation.

tests.name: History Truncation Control
tests.description: History length is truncated to a small window.

tests.name: Full History Run
tests.description: System transition depends on the complete accumulated history of deviations.

vectors.name: Markovian Sufficiency Check
vectors.attack: Compare divergence of full history runs against last-state-only control.
vectors.failure_condition: Divergence metrics and predictive gains from history are statistically insignificant (below epsilon threshold).
vectors.implication: The process can be fully modeled as a Markovian system, falsifying the non-Markov cumulative organization hypothesis.

maximum_supported_claim.statement: Admissibility dynamics exhibit historical dependence, wherein past deviation states condition future organization patterns beyond the last state.
